Other siblings: #5420 (app-shell designer save→publish), #5373 (`types`/`core`/`cli`, retiring `CRUDSchema`), #5247 (`core`/registry + `cli`, did-you-mean).

## 裁决 — maintainer ruling, ⛔ final, not to be re-adjudicated

Maintainer **huangyiirene**, 2026-08-12, on objectstack#7494 (comment `5261754173`), verbatim:

> 裁定:今天的合同就是 **org 级**;per-user scope 留在 #7611(v18),**不提前造**。
> console 停止把 sort / hiddenFields / columnState / rowHeight 呈现为「个人配置」,措辞与 UX 改为「**视图配置(对所有用户生效)**」;**写路径加权限门**(视图设计类权限),普通用户不再能替全组织重排视图。
> 路由:剩余工作全在 objectui(console 措辞/权限门 + `data-objectstack` 适配层),objectstack 侧无代码。

⚠️ This ruling sat **six days without an implementation card**. It is not a proposal; it is the contract.

## Scope — two halves of one contract change

1. **Wording/UX.** The console stops presenting `sort` / `hiddenFields` / `columnState` / `rowHeight` as *"persisted user preferences … per-view personal config"*. They are **view configuration that applies to all users of the view**, and the UI must say so where an operator can see it before acting.
2. **Permission gate.** The `updateViewConfig` write path is gated behind a **view-management-class** permission, so an ordinary user can no longer restyle a shared view **org-wide** from the toolbar.

## ⛔ Explicitly NOT in scope

- ⛔ **Per-user view config.** Parked in objectstack#7611 (v18; restart requires real customer demand). ⛔ **Do not build any per-user storage under this card** — not a fallback, not a feature flag, not a "while I'm here".
- ⛔ **`persistViewPatch` merged-base freezing** — a separate defect card from the same ruling line (「独立小修,现在做」).
- ⛔ The row-classification half — already done (objectui#4227 / PR #4713).

## PM mechanism assumptions — measure, do not inherit

1. ⚠️ **The line number is six days old.** `ObjectView.tsx ~1455` was measured when the card was filed; `packages/plugin-view` has moved since. Re-derive the wording site(s) by **searching for the prose**, not by line number, and report what you found. ⚠️ There may be **more than one** — the card says *"and any sibling prose"*, which is an admission that the census was not exhaustive. ✅ Do your own census and state its method.
2. ⚠️ **"A view-management-class permission" names a class, not a permission.** ⛔ Do not invent a permission name. Find what this repo already uses for view/designer-class authority, reach that, and say which one you chose and why. ⚠️ If no suitable permission exists, that is a **contract gap** and you ⛔ **stop and report** — minting a permission name is not a dev decision.
3. ⚠️ **A gate that only hides the button is not a gate.** The ruling says the **write path** is gated. Hiding the toolbar affordance while `updateViewConfig` still accepts the call leaves the org-wide write reachable by anything that calls the adapter. ✅ Gate the write; ⛔ do not settle for the affordance. If you also hide the affordance, say so as an addition, not as the fix.
4. ⚠️ **Measure what an ungated caller gets today, and what it gets after.** A refusal that is silent is the failure mode this lane has hit repeatedly this round (#5861, #5969). ✅ State, quoted, what a user without the permission now sees — and ⛔ if the answer is "the call quietly no-ops", that is not done.
5. ⚠️ **The wording change is user-visible text.** Check whether these strings are i18n keys before editing English in place; if they are, the change belongs in the locale packs and `check:i18n-keys` / `check:i18n-drift` become live gates for you.

## Verification

Predict the direction **before** running. The load-bearing legs: a **permitted** user still writes view config successfully, and an **unpermitted** user is **refused** — both in the same run, so "the gate works" cannot be satisfied by breaking the write for everyone.

⚠️ **Commit your own edit before you ablate** — measured on #5859 today: a `trap` restore using `git checkout --` reverted the dev's still-uncommitted edit along with the probe's mutation, and it **reported success both times**. ⛔ And note the sharper variant measured on #5674: **`git checkout <ref> -- <path>` writes the INDEX as well as the worktree**, so using it to read a baseline and then restoring with `git checkout -- <path>` restores *the baseline over your work*.

⚠️ **Five phantom-class defects were self-caught by devs on this round's cards**, all one root: *an assertion or control that cannot distinguish the two states of the world* — including one where a **shared mock object** carried a previous test's write into the next case and made it pass while measuring nothing. ✅ State explicitly **which of your assertions would still pass if your change were reverted**, and make each control a string present in **both** versions of the file.

⚠️ **A cached turbo green is not a measurement** — measured on #5852 today: an un-forced sweep reported 77/78 cached. Use `--force` on any turbo-run gate you treat as evidence.

Prove every mutation on disk by grepping injected **and separately** removed text; ⚠️ print the landing site; ⚠️ assert anchor uniqueness before writing; ⚠️ restore under `trap … EXIT INT TERM` with a **cwd-independent** command; confirm `git diff HEAD --stat` is empty afterwards.

**Gates by name, with exit codes:** `type-check` for every package touched (⚠️ hyphenated; echo the script name; distinguish the **unbuilt-closure** red from the **missing-`node_modules`** red; ⚠️ **build `./examples/**` too**, not just `./packages/**`), root-form vitest quoting per-test names, the downstream **prefix-form** sweep with the direction **demonstrated**, eslint with merge-base delta (⚠️ plain `eslint .`; ⛔ no `--no-inline-config`), plus `check:i18n-keys` / `check:i18n-drift` if item 5 applies.

⚠️ **Use `pnpm exec vitest run [paths]` from the repo root** — ⛔ **not** `pnpm --filter … test -- [paths]`, which silently drops everything after `--`. ⚠️ **Zero-match pnpm trap**: a filter matching nothing prints *"No projects matched the filters"* and exits **0**. Run `node scripts/check-changeset-presence.mjs` rather than guessing — ⚠️ **#6073 widened it beyond `/src/`** today. Changeset **`minor`** if a published signature changes, otherwise `patch`; ⛔ never `major`. ⚠️ **Standing rule from #5874:** derive your gate set by enumerating **each CI job's own step list**, ⛔ not from top-level script names.

## Deliverable

Draft PR, body with `Fixes #5232`. ⛔ Do not mark ready, ⛔ do not enqueue, ⛔ no auto-merge — the PM lands it. ⚠️ **Audit your PR body for closing keywords near any sibling issue number — GitHub's parser ignores negation**, so "filed, not fixed: #NNNN" still closes #NNNN (measured on #5674 today). Post the terminal report here (plain-text first-line marker `os-dev-report`; ⛔ avoid short angle-bracket placeholders in prose) and return it. State, per gate: command, exit code, what a red would have meant; your wording census and its method; which permission you gated on and why; what an unpermitted caller now sees, quoted; **which of your assertions would still pass on a revert**; and any deviation with its reason.
